extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, patent litigation researchers, and empirical legal researchers
extracted.subtask_description: An empirical, case-level study design and reporting rubric for measuring how the §285 attorneys' fees exceptionality standard (pre- and post-Octane) affected the rate and form of fee-shifting awards in patent litigation. Includes case selection, coding rules, categorical variables, and statistical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case filing timing (pre-certiorari filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include only cases filed before certiorari was granted in Octane so that all cases were filed with the assumption they met the pre-Octane attorneys’ fees standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: ensures cases were filed under the same initial standard. Practically implemented by selecting cases decided in defined windows (nine months before certiorari grant and nine months after Octane decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation windows (equal-length before/after intervals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select identical-length time intervals before and after Octane (nine months each) to capture many cases while limiting variation in governing §285 interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: controls for legal drift; nine-month interval chosen because the study started nine months following Octane. Use same interval length before and after to account for possible drift.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion — decision on §285 motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Include only decisions that actually decided an attorneys’ fees shifting motion under 35 U.S.C. §285; exclude cases that merely mention §285 in other contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation: read each returned case to determine whether it was deciding a §285 motion; eliminate cases mentioning §285 in unrelated discussions (e.g., Lanham Act references, discussion of other Patent Act provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data source and search strategy (WestlawNext)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use WestlawNext to find cases and record all cases citing 35 U.S.C. §285 during the time periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caveats: WestlawNext may miss opinions (e.g., very short opinions, unpublished orders), may vary by district or time, and may mis-tag statute mentions. Mitigation: also search for exact phrase '35 U.S.C. § 285' and combinations like 'patent' + 'attorneys' fees' to verify results; nonetheless dataset may be under-representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit of observation — one entry per motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat each motion for attorneys' fees as a distinct data entry; if a decision contains motions by multiple parties, create separate entries for each motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: study examines the §285 standard as applied to fee motions, not per-case aggregations. Avoid arbitrarily subdividing motions into parts; each motion is one unit even if it concerns multiple claims or time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success coding — any fees shifted = success
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of a party’s requested fees were shifted, the motion was recorded as successful and fees were considered shifted (partial awards count as success).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: movant expectations unknown; practical difficulty dividing motions; courts often decide fee-shifting as a whole. Thus partial grants treated the same as full grants for the primary rate metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording amount of fees — excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not record or analyze the monetary amount of fees shifted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: theoretical irrelevance of amount to meeting the §285 standard and practical unavailability of amounts in many opinions without deeper docket access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial fee-shifting detail recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether fee awards were partial and, if so, for which portion (e.g., certain claims, certain time periods, specific expenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: investigate whether judges exercise new Octane discretion via new forms of partial awards. Tabulate types of partial awards (only certain claims; only after discovery; only certain expenses; etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluding motions not adjudicated under exceptionality standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude motions that were not decided on the Octane exceptionality standard (e.g., where the defendant was not the prevailing party) from the comparative analysis of pre/post-Octane exceptionality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: to isolate change in §285 exceptionality standard, only include motions where that standard was applicable; exclude others so the before/after ratio reflects changes in exceptionality judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial reasoning / factor coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Read each motion/opinion and code which tests or factors the judge discussed (e.g., Brooks Furniture tests or similar) and whether the award was justified by those tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows analysis of (a) frequency of Brooks Furniture factor discussion pre/post, (b) which new factors are discussed post-Octane, and (c) frequency of reliance on new factors—useful to identify whether judges adjusted §285 decision-making processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical identifiers (judge, district, circuit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the judge who decided each case, the district, and the circuit in which the district sits to enable geographic comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare rates among judges/districts/circuits before and after Octane to observe categorical jurisprudential differences. Note: small sample sizes limit per-judge inference (most judges appear only once).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent technology classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Record U.S. classifications for the patents asserted and group them into broader technology categories (ELEC, INST, CHEM, PHAR, INDUS, MACH, CONS) plus a separate SOFT (software) category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OST (Observatoire des Sciences et Techniques) broad classifications as baseline; group many narrow classes into eight categories to allow comparison across technology types and to detect compositional confounding between periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Movant identity coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether the movant seeking fees was the patentee or the accused infringer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze whether relative rates of fee shifting differ between patentees and accused infringers and whether these differences changed pre/post-Octane, including within technology subgroups where data permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum sample size requirements for statistical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Require at least two elements in each sample (pre and post) for a category to compute a standard deviation and perform statistical analysis; omit categories with fewer than two observations in either period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a sample has only one element SD cannot be calculated; many districts/circuits/categories lacked sufficient motions so statistics were not performed for them. This constraint dictates which categorical breakdowns are reportable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical metrics reported (confidence intervals and probability of change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report 95% confidence intervals for sample parameters (e.g., rate of fee shifting) and report the likelihood/probability that the true value changed between pre- and post-Octane samples using Welch’s t-test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain CI meaning (95% chance a repeat sample mean would fall in interval). Use Welch’s two-sample t-test to test equality of means when variances differ. Provide caveats about interpretation with small samples (wide CIs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and exclusion of cases decided on other grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude motions decided on other procedural or substantive grounds (three cases pre-Octane and five post-Octane in this dataset) from the analysis of the Octane exceptionality standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These cases are not relevant to the change in the exceptionality standard and therefore removed so the comparison reflects only cases decided under that standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of motions with internal partiality (do not subdivide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not break motions into multiple counted parts when awards are partial (e.g., only certain claims or periods); treat the motion as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: practical difficulty (opinions often lack detail separating claims/time periods), inconsistency across cases, and courts often decide fee shifting as a whole unless an exceptional factor calls out portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting for WestlawNext coverage bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge possible biases from WestlawNext coverage (e.g., exclusion of short opinions, variable publication by district), which could under-represent actual §285 decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, use multiple searches (exact phrase, combined terms) to confirm capture; but accept that some decisions (orders without opinions, mis-tagged opinions) may be missing, and note this as a limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical aggregation rules (circuits/districts/technologies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only compute and report statistics for circuits/districts/technology groups that have multiple motions in both pre- and post-periods; omit groups lacking sufficient cross-period representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: to make meaningful before/after comparisons require at least two observations per period. Examples: many circuits omitted because they did not have at least two motions in both periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation caveats for small-sample inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly caution that small sample sizes produce wide confidence intervals and limit the legitimacy of statistical inferences; odd statistical artifacts (e.g., 0% ± 0% CI) may arise from insufficient data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise readers to treat district- and judge-level conclusions with caution; more data would be necessary for accurate and meaningful inferences in small subsamples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate reporting of fee-shifting rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Report overall rates (percentage) of motions shifting fees in whole or in part and of partial shifting, with sample standard deviations and 95% CIs for pre- and post-Octane samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example reported results: Pre-Octane any shifting 31% (SD 47%), Post-Octane 44% (SD 50%); compute probability of change (e.g., 82% chance standard changed) using Welch’s t-test.
